title: The Changing Earth
subtitle: Analyzing the stark realities and actionable transformations of our global climate

slides.title: The Anthropocene Shift
slides.subtitle: Comparing historical baselines with modern ecological realities
slides.imagePrompt: Side-by-side comparison split composition showing a lush green alpine glacier in 1980 on the left transitioning into a heavily receded rock and mud landscape with minimal ice patches in modern times on the right

leftSide.title: Historical Baseline (1900)
bullets: Stable polar ice caps maintaining global sea level equilibrium and reflecting solar radiation effectively
Predictable seasonal precipitation patterns supporting indigenous biodiversity and stable agricultural zones
Balanced atmospheric carbon concentrations operating within natural pre-industrial cyclical limits

rightSide.title: Contemporary Reality (Present)
bullets: Accelerated glacial retreat in Greenland and Antarctica driving unprecedented global sea level rise
Intensified extreme weather events including prolonged multi-year droughts and catastrophic flash flooding
Atmospheric carbon dioxide levels exceeding 420 ppm, triggering irreversible tipping points

slides.title: Oceanic Consequences
slides.subtitle: How rising temperatures and acidification reshape marine biomes
slides.imagePrompt: Split image showing vibrant multi-colored coral reef teeming with diverse fish life on one half, transitioning into bleached, white, lifeless coral skeleton on the murky ocean floor on the other half
bullets: Marine heatwaves cause widespread coral bleaching events, destroying vital breeding grounds for twenty-five percent of all marine species globally.
Increased carbon dioxide absorption leads to ocean acidification, dissolving the calcium carbonate shells of microscopic pteropods and crustaceans.
Expanding oceanic dead zones resulting from agricultural runoff and thermal stratification suffocate pelagic ecosystems and collapse fisheries.
Disruption of major thermal currents, such as the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation, threatens to radically alter global weather patterns.

slides.title: The Thermal Edge
slides.subtitle: Quantifying our proximity to irreversible planetary thresholds
slides.statLabel: Global Average Temperature Rise Above Pre-Industrial Levels
bullets: Every fraction of a degree exponentially increases the frequency of extreme heatwaves and agricultural failures.
The Paris Agreement threshold of 1.5 degrees Celsius is rapidly approaching within the next decade.
Mitigation efforts require halving global greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 to avoid catastrophic tipping points.

slides.title: Ecosystem Vulnerability Index
slides.subtitle: Assessing the critical stress points across Earth's major biomes
slides.imagePrompt: Before and after aerial photograph sequence showing dense Amazonian rainforest canopy on top transitioning into fragmented, burned deforested cattle pastureland on the bottom

cards.title: The Amazon Rainforest
cards.description: Facing a dangerous feedback loop where deforestation and rising temperatures transform the world's largest carbon sink into an arid savannah emitting more carbon than it absorbs.

cards.title: Arctic Permafrost
cards.description: Rapidly thawing sub-surface ground releases massive trapped reserves of methane and carbon dioxide, significantly accelerating the warming trajectory of the global atmosphere.

cards.title: Global Agricultural Belts
cards.description: Unpredictable monsoons, severe soil degradation, and chronic water scarcity threaten long-term food security for billions of people living in developing and developed nations alike.

slides.title: The Decarbonization Pathway
slides.subtitle: Strategic phases required to achieve net-zero global emissions
slides.imagePrompt: Futuristic urban landscape showing a smog-filled city skyline on the left transitioning into a clean, green, solar-powered eco-city with vertical forests and electric transit on the right

steps.title: Phase 1: Energy Transition
steps.subtitle: Fossil Fuel Phase-Out
steps.description: Rapidly decommission coal and gas power plants while aggressively scaling utility-scale solar, wind, and next-generation geothermal energy grids.

steps.title: Phase 2: Industrial Overhaul
steps.subtitle: Green Manufacturing
steps.description: Electrify heavy industrial processes, transition to green hydrogen for steel production, and revolutionize global supply chain logistics.

steps.title: Phase 3: Ecosystem Restoration
steps.subtitle: Natural Sinks
steps.description: Implement massive global reforestation, restore degraded wetlands, and adopt regenerative agricultural practices to draw down atmospheric carbon.

steps.title: Phase 4: Circular Economy
steps.subtitle: Resource Efficiency
steps.description: Redesign manufacturing for infinite recyclability, eliminate single-use materials, and drastically reduce consumer waste across all economic sectors.

slides.title: The Final Verdict
slides.subtitle: A decisive moment in human history
slides.statement: We are the first generation to fully understand climate change, and the last generation with a narrow window to stop its most catastrophic consequences.
slides.support: Action is no longer a matter of political choice, but of planetary survival.
